<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Tilapia, as sold from Kitwe mining area (streams and Kafue River) (mining-affected area) had total mercury higher at 14 µg/kg, against 8 µg/kg for Non-mining control area (Chilubula, Kasama) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shumba2025-tilapia-mercury-zambia-mining|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shumba T, Kayumba AV, Kalinda C, Mukosha M, Mbewe M, Mwila C, Handema R, Mwenye OJ, Mbewe M · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shumba2025-tilapia-mercury-zambia-mining">Assessment of total mercury (Hg) in soil, sediment, and tilapia fish (Oreochromis niloticus) and health risk assessment among residents of Kitwe mining area, Zambia</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science and Pollution Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shumba2025-tilapia-mercury-zambia-mining">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the tilapia came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.



<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as tilapia

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers tilapia in 4 forms kept separate in every comparison: tilapia, as sold (255 results), tilapia, dried (11 results), tilapia, peeled or flesh (11 results) and tilapia, cooked (9 <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-tilapia" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-tilapia-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of tilapia, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

data-shared-occurrence-methods><summary>Shared dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:tilapia-e2a18cd0d1e3:81fc68b9f5d3"><summary>HMI tilapia Pb reference · Tilapia, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:tilapia-e2a18cd0d1e3:81fc68b9f5d3"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI tilapia Pb reference · Tilapia, as sold. Tilapia, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤10</td><td>≤11.2</td><td>≤12.3</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤10</td><td>≤11.2</td><td>≤12.3</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>12 reference units; 2 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>10</td><td>50%</td></tr><tr><td>Sirisangarunroj et al. 2023</td><td>2</td><td>50%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for tilapia, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>2 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/sirisangarunroj2023-thai-fish-toxic-elements" class="internal" data-slug="sources/sirisangarunroj2023-thai-fish-toxic-elements" data-no-cite-meta>Sirisangarunroj et al. 2023</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:tilapia-e2a18cd0d1e3:81fc68b9f5d3</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:tilapia-f286bf4488d5:fbe0c2b4c94d"><summary>HMI tilapia Pb reference · Tilapia, as sold, dry weight</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:tilapia-f286bf4488d5:fbe0c2b4c94d"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI tilapia Pb reference · Tilapia, as sold, dry weight. Tilapia, as sold; Dry weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤1000</td><td>≤1000</td><td>≤1000</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤1000</td><td>≤1000</td><td>≤1000</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>4 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Mendoza et al. 2023</td><td>4</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for tilapia, as sold on a dry weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>FDA Total Diet Study is the only compatible sampling family for tilapia, cooked on this basis in the completed tilapia ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" data-no-cite-meta>FDA Total Diet Study</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:tilapia-f3f3df96f0d5:7e3c31f55e29</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><div hidden data-form-reasons><p data-reason="no_numeric_value_or_bound" data-title="Spread or extreme value only">The source reports only a percentile, range or maximum for these samples, with no mean or median to place against the reference. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach tilapia

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach tilapia comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Tilapia, as sold from 0.3 mg/L HgCl2 exposure, basal diet (experiment) had total mercury higher at 1,500 µg/kg, against 40 µg/kg for unexposed control, basal diet in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/zahran2023-mercury-tilapia-nannochloropsis|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Zahran E, Ahmed F, Hassan Z, Ibrahim I, Khaled AA, Palić D, El Sebaei MG · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/zahran2023-mercury-tilapia-nannochloropsis">Toxicity Evaluation, Oxidative, and Immune Responses of Mercury on Nile Tilapia: Modulatory Role of Dietary Nannochloropsis oculata</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Not reported</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/zahran2023-mercury-tilapia-nannochloropsis">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, tilapia, dried from Dry season control (Riyom) (mining-affected area) had nickel higher at 15 µg/kg, against 5 µg/kg for Rainy season control (Riyom) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/okonofua2024-mining-pits-cabbage-fish-nigeria|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Okonofua ES, Komolafe AS, Emeribe CN, Ogbomida ET, Butu AW · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/okonofua2024-mining-pits-cabbage-fish-nigeria">Analysis of Bioaccumulation of Heavy Metals in Water, Cabbage (Brassica oleracea var. capitata) and Tilapia Fish (Oreochromis niloticus) from Unreclaimed Mining Pits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Earth Sciences Pakistan</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/okonofua2024-mining-pits-cabbage-fish-nigeria">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A third study found that tilapia, as sold from Kitwe mining area (streams and Kafue River) (mining-affected area) had total mercury higher at 15 µg/kg, against 7 µg/kg for Non-mining control area (Chilubula, Kasama) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shumba2025-tilapia-mercury-zambia-mining|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shumba T, Kayumba AV, Kalinda C, Mukosha M, Mbewe M, Mwila C, Handema R, Mwenye OJ, Mbewe M · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shumba2025-tilapia-mercury-zambia-mining">Assessment of total mercury (Hg) in soil, sediment, and tilapia fish (Oreochromis niloticus) and health risk assessment among residents of Kitwe mining area, Zambia</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science and Pollution Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shumba2025-tilapia-mercury-zambia-mining">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, tilapia, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (1 µg/kg) and the highest in SEARO (2 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

In one study, lead across 5 groups of tilapia ranged from 580 µg/kg (landing site Migunga mitatu) to 730 µg/kg (landing site Oltukai); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/sawe2023-fish-metals-lake-manyara-tanzania|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Sawe S, Amasi A, Wynants M · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sawe2023-fish-metals-lake-manyara-tanzania">Assessment of Potentially Toxic Metals in Fish from Lake Manyara, Northern Tanzania</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sawe2023-fish-metals-lake-manyara-tanzania">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/zahran2023-mercury-tilapia-nannochloropsis|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Zahran E, Ahmed F, Hassan Z, Ibrahim I, Khaled AA, Palić D, El Sebaei MG · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/zahran2023-mercury-tilapia-nannochloropsis">Toxicity Evaluation, Oxidative, and Immune Responses of Mercury on Nile Tilapia: Modulatory Role of Dietary Nannochloropsis oculata</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Not reported</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/zahran2023-mercury-tilapia-nannochloropsis">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

A useful lot result names the form, the basis and a quantification limit well below the limit that applies.



<a id="procurement-and-process-control"></a>
## Buying and verifying tilapia

<a id="hmi-ing-028"></a>
<a id="what-origin-traceability-processing-and-analytical-information-should-a-buyer-request"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-029"></a>
<a id="which-control-or-specification-choices-are-supported-and-which-are-policy-choices-requiring-separate-justification"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-030"></a>
<a id="what-supplier-process-or-test-result-changes-should-trigger-investigation-or-requalification"></a>

No maximum level for metals in tilapia was verified from primary text for this page; buyers should confirm the limit that applies in the destination market.



<a id="finished-product-and-exposure-implications"></a>
## Exposure from tilapia

<a id="hmi-ing-031"></a>
<a id="how-do-inclusion-rate-processing-yield-preparation-and-other-ingredients-affect-a-finished-product-estimate"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-032"></a>
<a id="how-do-consumption-patterns-and-intended-populations-affect-dietary-exposure-interpretation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-033"></a>
<a id="what-conclusions-require-finished-product-measurements-or-a-separate-exposure-assessment"></a>

No source in the library converted tilapia concentrations into a verified estimate of intake for a defined population. Concentrations describe the food, not individual risk.



<a id="requirements-evidence-assessment-and-updates"></a>
## Evidence review and remaining gaps

<a id="hmi-ing-034"></a>
<a id="which-primary-regulatory-instruments-apply-to-this-exact-ingredient-form-species-market-and-date"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-035"></a>
<a id="what-searches-eligibility-decisions-source-families-and-appraisal-underpin-the-answers-and-certainty-judgments"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-036"></a>
<a id="what-remains-unresolved-when-was-each-answer-reviewed-and-what-changed-in-this-version"></a>

Every source record that names tilapia was decided on its content: 24 occurrence extracted, 24 records in all. The occurrence table renders every extracted result; held values remain visible with their reason.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.


<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Tilapia FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-tilapia" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-tilapia" data-question="What heavy metals are found in tilapia?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in tilapia?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, methylmercury, mercury, nickel, chromium, uranium, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, Se, Ba, Hg and Mg in tilapia, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cammilleri2025-marine-collagen-toxic-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cammilleri G, Tortorici M, Pantano L, Galluzzo FG, Pulvirenti A, Buscemi MD, Lo Dico GM, Macaluso A, Calabrese V, Jacob UM, Ferrantelli V · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cammilleri2025-marine-collagen-toxic-metals">Toxic metals and metalloids in collagen supplements of fish and jellyfish origin: Risk assessment for daily intake</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Open Medicine</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cammilleri2025-marine-collagen-toxic-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/islam2015-bangladesh-foods-heavy-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Islam MS, Ahmed MK, Habibullah-Al-Mamun M, Raknuzzaman M · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/islam2015-bangladesh-foods-heavy-metals">The concentration, source and potential human health risk of heavy metals in the commonly consumed foods in Bangladesh</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Ecotoxicology and Environmental Safety</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/islam2015-bangladesh-foods-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported lead in tilapia, as sold from 150 results in 2 reporting regions, with subgroup medians from 1 to 2 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-tilapia" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-tilapia" data-question="How do heavy metals get into tilapia?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into tilapia?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, tilapia from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than tilapia from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shumba2025-tilapia-mercury-zambia-mining|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shumba T, Kayumba AV, Kalinda C, Mukosha M, Mbewe M, Mwila C, Handema R, Mwenye OJ, Mbewe M · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shumba2025-tilapia-mercury-zambia-mining">Assessment of total mercury (Hg) in soil, sediment, and tilapia fish (Oreochromis niloticus) and health risk assessment among residents of Kitwe mining area, Zambia</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science and Pollution Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shumba2025-tilapia-mercury-zambia-mining">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Tilapia, as sold from Kitwe mining area (streams and Kafue River) (mining-affected area) had total mercury higher at 14 µg/kg, against 8 µg/kg for Non-mining control area (Chilubula, Kasama) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shumba2025-tilapia-mercury-zambia-mining|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shumba T, Kayumba AV, Kalinda C, Mukosha M, Mbewe M, Mwila C, Handema R, Mwenye OJ, Mbewe M · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shumba2025-tilapia-mercury-zambia-mining">Assessment of total mercury (Hg) in soil, sediment, and tilapia fish (Oreochromis niloticus) and health risk assessment among residents of Kitwe mining area, Zambia</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science and Pollution Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shumba2025-tilapia-mercury-zambia-mining">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-tilapia" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-tilapia" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in tilapia?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in tilapia?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, tilapia, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (1 µg/kg) and the highest in SEARO (2 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-tilapia-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-tilapia-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in tilapia is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in tilapia is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 1 result from 1 source, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported inorganic arsenic in tilapia, as sold from 1 result in 1 reporting region, with subgroup medians below 20 µg/kg, mostly non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
